title: fix: log actual H2O hyperparameter values instead of constructor defa…
body:
## Summary

  The H2O model schemas log each hyperparameter via `value_attr`, which resolves to
  `getattr(model, "<param>")`. For a model retrieved from a grid search
  (`h2o.get_model`), the H2O attribute getters return the estimator's **constructor
  defaults**, not the values the model was actually built with. As a result,
  experiments logged for grid-search models all record identical, default
  hyperparameters even though each model used different values. The correct
  per-model values are only present inside the `actual_params` mapping.

  ## Change

  - Add a `value_key` directive to the schema logger. It resolves a value from a
    dict-valued attribute — `value_source`, defaulting to `actual_params` — and
    falls back to plain attribute access when the mapping is absent or does not
    contain the key (preserving existing `value_attr` behavior).
  - Repoint the individual hyperparameters in the H2O estimator schemas (GBM, RF,
    GLM, XGBoost, TargetEncoder) from `value_attr` to `value_key`, so logged values
    reflect each model's actual resolved parameters.
  - `h2o__ModelBase` (`actual_params`, `model_id`) and `h2o__H2OGenericEstimator`
    (`path`, `model_key`) are unchanged, as those are not grid-search hyperparameters.

  ## Behavior

  - **Single trained models:** effectively unchanged — `actual_params` matches the
    trained values, and the logic falls back to attribute access if the mapping is
    unavailable.
  - **Grid-search models:** individual hyperparameter values now reflect each
    model's actual parameters instead of constructor defaults.

  ## Tests

  Added unit tests for `value_key`: reading from the source mapping, falling back to
  attribute access when the key is absent or the mapping is missing, and honoring a
  custom `value_source`.

title: refactor(WIP): client layer migration to new repository interface
body:
# refactor: client layer migration to new repository interface

*This will only be merged once #593 makes it to `main`. For a clean diff against the repository refactor, see https://github.com/capitalone-contributions/rubicon-ml/pull/2.*

## Summary

Migrates the client layer from manually iterating multiple repositories (33 loops across 6 files) to calling a single repository directly. Slims `RepositoryBase` from 38 methods to 13. Adds `Rubicon.compose()` and `__add__` operator for intuitive multi-backend composition.

**Motivation**: The client layer duplicated multi-backend fan-out logic in every method — 33 `for repo in self.repositories` loops with inconsistent error handling. `CompositeRepository` (introduced in https://github.com/capitalone/rubicon-ml/pull/593) already handles broadcast/failover at the repository layer, but the client wasn't using it. Additionally, `RepositoryBase` carried ~25 convenience methods that every backend had to override, when most of those are simple dispatches that belong in the client.

## What changed

### `RepositoryBase` slimmed

| | Before (https://github.com/capitalone/rubicon-ml/pull/593) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Abstract methods | 8 | 8 (unchanged) |
| Convenience methods | ~30 | 5 (`create_project`, `get_project`, `get_projects`, `create_artifact`, `create_dataframe`) |
| Total methods | ~38 | 13 |

The ~25 removed convenience methods (`create_experiment`, `get_metric`, `add_tags`, etc.) are replaced by the client calling abstract methods directly:
```python
# Before
repo.create_metric(metric, project_name, experiment_id)

# After
repo.write_domain(metric, project_name, experiment_id=..., entity_identifier=..., entity_type="Metric")
```

### Backend simplification

- **`FsspecRepository`** — removed 9 convenience overrides (tags, comments, create_feature/metric/parameter). Existence checks for Feature/Metric/Parameter moved into `write_domain` dispatch.
- **`WandBRepository`** — removed 6 tag/comment overrides. Added `TagUpdate`/`CommentUpdate` handling to `write_domain` and `read_domains` (including W&B native `run.tags` sync).
- **`CompositeRepository`** — removed 12 convenience overrides. Only keeps `create_project`, `create_artifact`, `create_dataframe`, `get_projects`, `_get_artifact_data_path`, `finish`.

### Client single-repository pattern

Every client method now calls `self.repository.<method>(...)` once:
```python
# Before
for repo in self.repositories:
    repo.create_experiment(experiment)

# After
self.repository.write_domain(experiment, self.name, experiment_id=experiment.id)
```

`Rubicon` always holds a single `._config` with one `.repository` — either a direct backend or a `CompositeRepository`.

### New composition API

```python
# Class method
rb = Rubicon.compose(rb_local, rb_wandb)

# Operator (immutable, left = primary)
rb = rb_local + rb_wandb

# Chaining
rb = rb_local + rb_s3 + rb_wandb

# Existing API still works (for now)
rb = Rubicon(composite_config=[
    {"persistence": "filesystem", "root_dir": "/local"},
    {"persistence": "memory", "root_dir": "/mem"},
])
```

### Deprecations

- `Rubicon.configs` — returns `[self._config]`, emits `DeprecationWarning`
- `Rubicon.repositories` — returns `[self.repository]`, emits `DeprecationWarning`
- `Base.repositories` — same

## Test plan

- [x] 497 unit + regression tests pass
- [x] All test mock targets updated from removed methods to abstract methods (`read_domain`, `read_domains`, etc.)
- [x] Multi-backend error tests updated to expect `CompositeRepository` error messages
- [x] New tests: `test_rubicon_compose`, `test_rubicon_add_operator`, `test_rubicon_add_immutable`, `test_rubicon_add_chaining`, `test_composite_config_uses_composite_repository`, `test_rubicon_compose_full_crud`
- [x] Lint clean (`ruff check` + `ruff format`)

## Breaking changes

- **Repository convenience methods removed** — code that calls `repo.create_experiment(...)`, `repo.get_metric(...)`, `repo.add_tags(...)`, etc. directly on a repository instance must migrate to the abstract methods (`write_domain`, `read_domain`, `read_domains`). The user-facing client API (`project.log_experiment()`, `experiment.log_metric()`, etc.) is **unchanged**.
- **`Rubicon.repositories`** — deprecated. Returns `[self.repository]`. Use `.repository` instead.
- **`Rubicon.configs`** — deprecated. Returns `[self._config]`. Use `.config` instead.
- **Mock targets in tests** — patches targeting `FsspecRepository.get_metrics`, `FsspecRepository.get_experiments`, etc. must target `FsspecRepository.read_domains` or `FsspecRepository.read_domain` instead.

---

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code

This refactor was designed and [initially developed](https://github.com/capitalone/rubicon-ml/tree/refactor/repository-layer) over a year ago without the use of genAI. Due to diverging nearly 50 commits in both directions, we've used Claude Code to re-apply the refactor on that branch to one newly cut from the latest main. This PR will be thoroughly reviewed against the original implementation before removing from draft status.

title: refactor(WIP): repository layer abstraction
body:
# refactor: repository layer abstraction

## Summary

Introduces a clean abstract base class (`RepositoryBase`) for the repository layer, enabling new backends to be implemented with 8 methods instead of 50+. Extracts filesystem logic into `FsspecRepository`, rewrites `WandBRepository` to inherit the ABC directly, and adds a `CompositeRepository` for multi-backend fan-out.

**Motivation**: The previous `BaseRepository` mixed filesystem concerns (fsspec, path construction, JSON serialization) with the abstract repository interface. Every new backend had to override ~50 methods — `WandBRepository` was 1,330 lines of mostly stubs and reimplemented logic. This made API-based backends impractical to build and maintain.

## What changed

### New classes

- **`RepositoryBase(ABC)`** — 8 abstract methods (`write_domain`, `read_domain`, `read_domains`, `remove_domain`, `write_artifact_data`, `read_artifact_data`, `write_dataframe_data`, `read_dataframe_data`) + ~30 concrete convenience methods with the existing V1 names (`create_project`, `get_experiment`, etc.)

- **`FsspecRepository(RepositoryBase)`** — all filesystem logic extracted from the old `BaseRepository`. Implements the 8 abstracts using fsspec. Subclasses (`LocalRepository`, `S3Repository`, `MemoryRepository`) still only implement `_persist_bytes` and `_persist_domain`.

- **`CompositeRepository(RepositoryBase)`** — wraps multiple backends. Writes broadcast to all (primary errors propagate, secondary errors warn). Reads failover in priority order. Deep-copies domain objects to prevent mutation side-effects across heterogeneous backends.

- **`TagUpdate` / `CommentUpdate`** — domain dataclasses formalizing the existing on-disk event-sourced tag/comment format. No storage format change.

### Refactored classes

- **`WandBRepository`** — now inherits `RepositoryBase` directly (not `FsspecRepository`). Zero fsspec references. Implements 8 abstract methods + ~10 convenience overrides. **Down from 1,330 lines to ~780 lines.**

### Three-level override strategy

The abstraction has three levels:
1. **8 abstract methods** — what every backend MUST implement
2. **~30 convenience methods** (reduced further in #598) — default compositions that work for most backends
3. **Selective overrides** — backends override specific convenience methods where the default doesn't fit (e.g., `FsspecRepository.create_project` adds existence checks, `WandBRepository.create_artifact` mutates artifact IDs)

### Inheritance hierarchy

```
RepositoryBase (ABC)
├── FsspecRepository
│   ├── LocalRepository
│   │   └── MemoryRepository
│   └── S3Repository
├── WandBRepository
└── CompositeRepository
```

## Test plan

- [x] All existing unit tests pass (mock patch targets updated from `BaseRepository` → `FsspecRepository`)
- [x] All existing regression tests pass (filesystem, dataframe)
- [x] All WandB integration tests pass (28/28 against real W&B)
- [x] New `test_repository_base_abc.py` — 30 tests verifying ABC contract and convenience method delegation
- [x] New `test_wandb_repo.py` — 36 mocked tests covering structure, all 8 abstracts, convenience overrides, helpers
- [x] New `test_composite_repo.py` — 29 tests covering construction, broadcast, failover, full CRUD, heterogeneous mutation safety

## Breaking changes

- External, custom repository implementations that subclass `BaseRepository` directly will no longer work as `BaseRepository` has been removed. Users should migrate to `FsspecRepository` or `RepositoryBase`.
- Code that patches `rubicon_ml.repository.BaseRepository.<method>` in tests needs to patch `rubicon_ml.repository.FsspecRepository.<method>` instead.
- `WandBRepository` no longer exposes filesystem helpers (`_cat`, `_exists`, `_glob`, etc.). These were always stubs that raised — no real functionality lost.

---

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code

This refactor was designed and [initially developed](https://github.com/capitalone/rubicon-ml/tree/refactor/repository-layer) over a year ago without the use of genAI. Due to diverging nearly 50 commits in both directions, we've used Claude Code to re-apply the refactor on that branch to one newly cut from the latest main. This PR will be thoroughly reviewed against the original implementation before removing from draft status.
